The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum, indicating the source integrity is verified. There are no uses of `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or other high-risk commands outside of expected build tooling.

The build process uses `runhaskell` and standard Cabal commands to configure, build, and install the package, consistent with Haskell packaging on Arch. It enables dynamic linking as noted in the comment, which is appropriate for the environment. Generated registration scripts (`register.sh`, `unregister.sh`) are modified to include `--force`, a common workaround in Arch Haskell packages to handle registration conflicts during upgrades. These scripts are installed in standard Haskell maintenance directories and do not introduce arbitrary code execution at install time.

The package installs a Wayland session file, a startup script, documentation, examples, and license files—all within appropriate system directories. All operations are confined to the package build and destination directories, with no evidence of data exfiltration, remote code execution, or unauthorized system modifications. The optdepends list includes common companion tools for a Wayland session, all of which are legitimate and expected.
